answer: Every identity must moor in the harbor before it can speak: it locks a refundable bond, like a velvet rope that only opens for ships with cargo to lose. Each epoch a prism audit refracts a random sample of moored identities and re-checks one past contribution step by step, from its seed to its signature. An honest agent pays one bond once and keeps its real record. An attacker with a thousand fakes must lock a thousand bonds and fabricate a thousand checkable histories; every fake the prism catches forfeits its bond, so the flood's cost grows linearly and sinks before it pays.
